clue.text: Prepared a couple by day

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
D is the standard abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: A pair of people got themselves ready during the daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace yourself is to steel or ready yourself, so braced means made ready for an impact or ordeal.

clue.text: Browbeat an employer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to order someone about
second meaning: the person in charge at work

explanation.surface: Someone intimidates the person who hires them.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to domineer over people; as a noun it is the head of a workplace.

clue.text: Greed shown by artist falling back into a bad habit

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: into tells us one piece goes inside the words that follow it

parts.note: a vice is a bad habit

indicators.note: in a down entry, falling back means the word runs the wrong way round

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter relapses into a vice, and greed is the result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bad habit' supplies both A and VICE; the reversed artist sits inside VICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is the formal word for an excessive desire for wealth, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Takes out old pamphlets

parts.note: ex- means former
tracts are short pamphlets, often religious

explanation.surface: Someone removes some antique leaflets from a pile.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract something is to pull or draw it out, so the verb matches 'takes out' in tense and person.

clue.text: Game, dears, is arranged after tea

indicators.note: after places the rearranged piece behind the next one in the answer

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: arranged suggests letters set out in a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tells friends a party game is set up for after tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British slang for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a party game in which players act out titles for others to guess.

clue.text: Maybe hero Graham at one point was bleeding

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters given are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: letters taken as written
E, east, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: A man named Graham, a hero, was at one stage losing blood.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass point E joins the name before the letters are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A haemorrhage is an escape of blood from a ruptured vessel, so it is a noun for bleeding.

clue.text: Exhaust the Queen, coming up first to go to bed

indicators.note: first puts this piece at the start of the answer
in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen
to tire someone is to exhaust them

explanation.surface: Tiring out the monarch, who rises first and then heads off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire is the formal phrase for heading off for the night to sleep.

clue.text: Inactive worker at last given place to sleep

indicators.note: at last sets this piece at the end of the answer

parts.note: short for dormitory
the worker ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: An idle employee is finally given a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dormant describes something asleep or not currently active, like a volcano.

clue.text: Docker found in store without first wife and daughter

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so these words wrap around the rest

parts.note: taken as written
Eve, wife of Adam, was the first wife in the Bible
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A dock worker turns up in a shop without his spouse and child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore loads and unloads ships, the same job as a dock worker.

clue.text: Read Tory extremists, just a few

parts.note: to scan a page is to read it

indicators.note: extremists suggests only the outermost letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Tory

explanation.surface: A few hardline Conservatives can read.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means meagre or barely enough, close to the sense of 'just a few'.

clue.text: No accommodation charge for new referent

definitions.note: a noun phrase; the answer is an adjective meaning without that charge

indicators.note: new suggests the letters made into something different

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A newcomer who was referred is promised free lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Living rent-free means occupying a home without paying the landlord anything.

clue.text: Steal mobile phone card back, which is fitting

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: the SIM card in a mobile phone
appropriate means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: Someone pinches a phone and returns the card, which seems only right.
explanation.definitionFit: To misappropriate is to take funds or property dishonestly for your own use, a form of theft.

clue.text: Consider in advance how it permeated working

indicators.note: working suggests letters in motion, rearranged into a new form

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Planning ahead about how something seeped through while in operation.
explanation.definitionFit: To premeditate is to think out or plan something beforehand, as with a crime.

clue.text: Touching sentiment, darling

parts.note: a sweet gesture is a touching one
the heart stands for feeling or sentiment

explanation.surface: A moving feeling addressed to a loved one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweetheart and darling are both affectionate terms for a loved one.

clue.text: Sort of single schism (not hard) producing gaffes

indicators.note: sort of suggests a version of the letters sorted into another order
not tells us a letter is left out of the word

parts.note: sole means single or only
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A kind of split in a group produces blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Solecisms are errors of grammar or etiquette, social or verbal gaffes.

clue.text: Getting back to the office initially with a German fellow

indicators.note: getting back means the word is turned to read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Returning to work early with a colleague from Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, as of Bismarck.

clue.text: Fifty, say, are educated

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to iterate is to say again

explanation.surface: People in their fifties, for instance, are well schooled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example'; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A literate person can read and write, and more widely is well educated.

clue.text: Want some blacking

indicators.note: some means only part of the next word is used, its letters running on

parts.note: found inside the word

explanation.surface: Needing a bit of boot polish.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in its older sense means absence or shortage, the same as a deficiency.

clue.text: Clerical staff?

parts.note: surface reading: office clerks and secretaries
setter's reading: a literal staff, a rod, carried by a churchman

explanation.walkthrough: Clerical means both of office clerks and of the clergy; staff means both employees and a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A crozier is the hooked staff carried by a bishop as a symbol of pastoral office.

clue.text: Iced tea tap: replaced top

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put back in different places

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A cafe's iced-tea dispenser has had its lid swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like a noun for a lid; it is the slang verb meaning to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: To top someone is slang for to kill them, and decapitate means to behead, removing the head or top.

clue.text: Pressure hosepipe for transport company

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hose carrying compressed air
second meaning: a firm operating passenger flights

explanation.surface: A firm that moves goods orders a high-pressure hose.
explanation.definitionFit: An air line is a tube for compressed air, and an airline is a company flying passengers.

clue.text: Ten feed on an antiseptic

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means this piece sits above the next

parts.note: ten is written 10, which looks like the letters I and O
to dine is to eat or feed

explanation.surface: Ten of them dose themselves with a disinfectant.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine, in tincture, is a familiar antiseptic for cuts and grazes.

clue.text: Show of hypocrisy when crawler gets damages

parts.note: a crocodile crawls along on its belly
to tear something is to damage it

explanation.surface: A toady who suffers losses puts on false sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' looks like a sycophant but is the reptile; 'damages' is a verb, not compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile tears are insincere grief, a fake display of feeling, from the myth that crocodiles weep while eating prey.

clue.text: Animal's pelt?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long-eared mammal like a large rabbit
second meaning: to run very fast, as in pelt down the road

explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal's pelt' suggests a skin; the 's is 'is', and pelt is the verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names the fast-running mammal, and the verb means to dash at speed.

clue.text: Lucid as I, maybe, yet self-destructive

indicators.note: maybe hints that the letters given are one possible order among many

parts.note: letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be as clear-headed as the speaker, yet bent on ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Suicidal behaviour is literally or figuratively likely to destroy oneself.

clue.text: Spoil one article overturned in dock

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A boat capsized at its mooring, ruining something.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour with moorings for yachts, a dock for pleasure boats.

clue.text: Wizard's church swamped by false errors

indicators.note: something swamped is engulfed, so it sits inside the other piece
false suggests the letters are not in their true order

parts.note: letters taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wizard's church is overwhelmed by mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorcerer is a magician who practises spells, another word for a wizard.

clue.text: About to surrender in retreat

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to cede is to give up or surrender

explanation.surface: A force on the point of giving in while falling back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw, as floodwater or a hairline does.
